questions.q: How does a prompt's output differ from a category classification model's output?
options: They are identical in every way
A prompt generates new text shaped by your instructions; a classifier picks from categories you predefined
A prompt can only return numbers
A classifier generates new text; a prompt returns a category
questions.explain: Classification restricts output to predefined categories. A prompt generates new, original text based on plain-language instructions you wrote.

questions.q: What underlying service actually runs AI Builder prompts?
options: A locally hosted open-source model with no cloud dependency
GPT model versions powered by Azure OpenAI Service
Azure SQL Database
Power BI's AI visuals engine
questions.explain: AI Builder prompts run on GPT model versions powered by Azure OpenAI Service, which is part of the broader Azure AI family.

questions.q: What is the current name of the flow action used to call a prompt, as of May 2025?
options: Create text with GPT using a prompt (unchanged)
Summarize content
Run a prompt
Generate AI response
questions.explain: The action was renamed from 'Create text with GPT using a prompt' to 'Run a prompt' in May 2025.

questions.q: A prompt named 'Summarize Support Email' has an input called EmailBody. How do you supply that input inside a flow?
options: It fills in automatically with no configuration
By filling it with dynamic content, such as the email body from a trigger, exactly like any other action's input
You must hardcode the text at design time and can never change it
Inputs can't be mapped from a trigger, only from a static value
questions.explain: A prompt's defined inputs appear in the flow designer and are filled with dynamic content the same way you'd wire up any other action's input field.

questions.q: After Run a prompt generates a summary into its Text output variable, what can you do with that variable?
options: Nothing — prompt outputs can't be reused
Only display it inside AI Builder's own interface
Use it as dynamic content in any downstream action that accepts text, such as posting it to Teams or writing it to a spreadsheet
It must first be converted using a separate Parse JSON action
questions.explain: The generated Text output is plain dynamic content, usable in any later action that accepts a text input — no special conversion required.
